item.title: Shopkeepers raise alarm over unpaid teachers forced to buy on credit, FTA members could call for industrial action
item.description: Shopkeepers have been calling the Fijian Teachers Association to raise concerns about teachers who are being forced to buy goods on credit because they have not received their salaries, and FTA's members could call for industrial action if the issue remains unresolved. This has been shared to fijivillage News by the General Secretary of the Fiji Teachers Association, Paula Manumanunitoga.
item.content:encoded:
Shopkeepers have been calling the Fijian Teachers Association to raise concerns about teachers who are being forced to buy goods on credit because they have not received their salaries, and FTA's members could call for industrial action if the issue remains unresolved.

This has been shared to fijivillage News by the General Secretary of the Fiji Teachers Association, Paula Manumanunitoga.

He says the failure to pay workers on time is a serious concern under the Employment Relations Act.

Manumanunitoga says the situation is extremely serious, with some teachers going for several months without getting paid after taking up appointments, particularly those posted to the outer islands.

According to Manumanunitoga, newly appointed teachers receive their appointment letters and travel to their assigned schools, often having to make arrangements to reach remote communities by boat however, some reportedly wait one, two, three, or even four months before receiving their first salary.

He says in some cases, teachers have accumulated nearly $1,000 in credit.

Manumanunitoga says once a person has been appointed and begins working, they are expected to receive their salaries.

He says the association has questioned why the current backlog has occurred, noting that in the past, appointment letters were sent directly to the relevant salaries section so that payments can be processed.

The General Secretary says following discussions with the Permanent Secretary, the association was given an undertaking that teachers who have not received their salaries would be paid in Pay 17.

The association is calling for those responsible for the delays to be identified and held accountable, saying the situation cannot be allowed to continue.

There is also growing concern about what could happen if teachers are not paid as promised.

The FTA is urging the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Finance to ensure that all outstanding salaries, including acting allowances, are paid as promised.

Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro highlighted earlier this week that salary arrears owed to 318 Ministry of Education staff will be expedited and processed through Pay 17 and Pay 18.

Radrodro assured all affected teachers and Ministry of Education staff that the necessary processes are underway to facilitate the payment of these outstanding salary arrears.

He acknowledged the concerns and difficulties experienced by staff as a result of the delays.

The Minister says these delays have been due to internal processing and compliance requirements necessary to ensure that all payments are properly verified and processed accurately and efficiently.

He says to support the timely processing of payments, all affected teachers are encouraged to ensure that their documentation is complete and up to date, including proper appointment documentation, FTRA registration certificates, correct bank account details and confirmation of commencement dates from Heads of Schools and/or District Education Officers.

He says the Ministry has undertaken the necessary due diligence to ensure that appointments are properly formalised and that all required documentation is in place before payments are processed.

Radrodro says welfare of their staff remains a priority for the Ministry.

Charters' 7 devices re-seized by Police, High Court motion filed after the seizure
item.description: Fijian and British national, Charlie Charters has filed a High Court motion after the Fiji Police Force returned seven seized electronic devices to Charters’ lawyer on Friday after the investigation against him was ended in the High Court, only for Fiji Police to immediately re-seize them under a fresh court order. The seven devices include medical apps for the treatment and management of Charters
item.content:encoded:
Fijian and British national, Charlie Charters has filed a High Court motion after the Fiji Police Force returned seven seized electronic devices to Charters’ lawyer on Friday after the investigation against him was ended in the High Court, only for Fiji Police to immediately re-seize them under a fresh court order.

The seven devices include medical apps for the treatment and management of Charters’ throat cancer and heart condition that he has not been able to access for six months, as well as financial and payment Apps and hard drives on which his work product is stored.

Charters says you have always got to be braced for Fiji’s capacity to surprise but even they were shocked by what happened to his lawyer, Seforan Fatiaki when he presented himself to CID on Friday.

He says the investigation by FICAC has been thoroughly discredited in the High Court so it seems truly bizarre where this is going now.

Fatiaki had first applied to FICAC in writing for the return of the devices on March 16th.

In court on Friday August 7th, Magistrate Shageeth Somaratne ordered the Fiji Police to return the devices to Charters’ lawyer.

The devices had been seized a day after FICAC’s February 21st detention and arrest at Nadi Airport, and their subsequent charging of Charters, which was permanently stayed by the High Court on July 24th.

Charters says the Police do not appear to have understood Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu’s ruling.

He says the charges against him were stayed by the High Court for a number of reasons including that, in the absence of any law limiting his rights, we all enjoy the right of freedom of speech, expression, thought, opinion and publication under section 17 of the Constitution.

Charters says the judge has said that when expressing those rights, we also have the right not to divulge the sources of our journalistic information.

He also alleges there were significant errors in the search warrant documentation which would be part of the submissions that would be argued in the High Court action.

item.title: Police lead, RFMF provides support in joint operations - Tikoduadua
item.description: The Republic of Fiji Military Forces remains in a supporting role as it conducts joint operations with the Fiji Police Force, with police continuing to take the lead on the ground. Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua says the arrangement is not new, with the RFMF stepping in when additional manpower and specialised capabilities are required.
item.content:encoded:
The Republic of Fiji Military Forces remains in a supporting role as it conducts joint operations with the Fiji Police Force, with police continuing to take the lead on the ground.

Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua says the arrangement is not new, with the RFMF stepping in when additional manpower and specialised capabilities are required.

INSERT: Minister on RFMF provides support PN 13th Aug

Tikoduadua says while joint operations involving the RFMF can be expensive, the military has capabilities that can provide critical support when needed.

He highlighted the use of drones by the Republic of Fiji Navy , particularly during search and rescue operations where visibility and weather conditions allow them to be deployed.

item.title: Bainimarama and Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum meet Truth and Reconciliation Commission Chair
item.description: Former Prime Minister, Voreqe Bainimarama and former Attorney General, Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum have met with the Chairman of the Fiji Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Joaquim Da Fonseca. Sayed-Khaiyum has posted a photo, saying it was a pleasure meeting the Chair of the Reconciliation Commission.
item.content:encoded:
Former Prime Minister, Voreqe Bainimarama and former Attorney General, Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum have met with the Chairman of the Fiji Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Joaquim Da Fonseca.

Sayed-Khaiyum has posted a photo, saying it was a pleasure meeting the Chair of the Reconciliation Commission.

He says they had an engaging discussion and they appreciate his efforts.

The Truth and Reconciliation Commission was hoping to get targeted submissions from all the coup leaders and former leaders.

We are currently trying to confirm on whether Bainimarama and Sayed-Khaiyum will appear before the commission or make a submission.

item.title: Woman accused of assaulting university student on bus admitted to St Giles Hospital
item.description: The woman who allegedly assaulted a 20-year-old university student on a bus travelling from Laucala Beach to Suva last week, has been admitted to St Giles Hospital. Police have confirmed that she will be interviewed once a doctor declares her fit for an interview.
item.content:encoded:
The woman who allegedly assaulted a 20-year-old university student on a bus travelling from Laucala Beach to Suva last week, has been admitted to St Giles Hospital.

Police have confirmed that she will be interviewed once a doctor declares her fit for an interview.

In a video sent to fijivillage News by a relative of the student, the woman was seen pulling the younger woman's hair.

She then got out of her seat, appeared to have a verbal argument with other passengers, walked to the front of the bus, pushed another female high school student out of her seat, and then got off the bus.

The relative said her nose was bleeding, her face was scratched, and she hit the back of her head on the metal part of a bus seat during the incident.

He said it was an unprovoked attack and they do not know each other.

item.content:encoded:
Yat Sen Primary School welcomed a Chinese delegation that spent a week teaching students about the richness of Chinese culture through dance, music, art, and other cultural activities.

ThepPrimary school students today showcased what they learnt within 1 week from the 14 teachers that came from the province of Yunnan Language and Culture College in China. The items included martial arts, painting, music and dances.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Assistant Head Teacher Meli Yabakivou says the cultural event plays an important role in the holistic development of students by helping them understand and appreciate the different cultures represented within the school community.

Yabakivou, who hails from Tailevu, says the school embraces students from diverse religious and cultural backgrounds and believes such programmes promote understanding and respect among students.

He added that the school was fortunate to have the Chinese delegation visit and share their culture and knowledge with the students.

Yabakivou thanked the Chinese Embassy and the parents and guardians of the school for helping the students during this transition.

item.title: Fiji-Canada partnership creates international opportunities for young Fijian dancers
item.description: Young Fijian dancers are gaining international exposure and opportunities for stronger artistic practice and development through a five-year partnership between Fiji’s Conservatorium of Dance, funded by the VOU Foundation, and Canada’s Arch-Way Dance. The partnership is based on a reciprocal model of travel, artistic training and community integration, with dancers from both countries having oppor
item.content:encoded:
Young Fijian dancers are gaining international exposure and opportunities for stronger artistic practice and development through a five-year partnership between Fiji’s Conservatorium of Dance, funded by the VOU Foundation, and Canada’s Arch-Way Dance.

The partnership is based on a reciprocal model of travel, artistic training and community integration, with dancers from both countries having opportunities to learn and share their artistic experiences.

This year, a 45-member delegation from Mission, British Columbia, comprising 15 young dancers aged 10 to 16 and 30 family members, arrived in Nadi for a 10-day cultural exchange.

The Canadian dancers are training alongside first-year students from the Conservatorium of Dance, Fiji’s pioneering dance academy, taking part in daily four-hour intensive training modules over the 10 days, led by Fijian instructors Navi Fong, David and Patrick.

Director of VOU and the Conservatorium of Dance, Sachiko Soro says the collaboration is important because it is building bridges of cultural connection and providing room for stronger artistic practice and development.

Soro says it is so wonderful to have 45 Canadians here in Fiji, 15 of them young dancers who are sharing, learning and giving their artistic selves with the Conservatorium of Dance students.

She says the exchange is just as important when Fijian artists travel to Canada, as they did last year.

She says in 2025, five Fijian artists from VOU travelled to Canada, where they led community workshops and performed at the Mission Folk Music Festival, with their showcases celebrated as festival highlights.

Soro says the current exchange in Nadi began at the VOU Dance Studios with a traditional Fijian sevusevu ceremony.

She says a significant cross-cultural moment occurred when an Indigenous family member from the Canadian delegation offered the formal protocol response.

The Canadian dancers are being immersed in Fijian culture while working alongside Conservatorium students, with the programme combining technical movement training with the mana and spirit of Fijian heritage.

Arch-Way Dance Director Gina Mataika says the core vision is to immerse the dancers in an experience that is rich in culture and provides a meaningful alternative to competitive dance.

Mataika says the experience has pushed the dancers out of their comfort zones and taught them the true meaning of perseverance.

She says they are growing not just as performers, but as individuals.

Mataika says the knowledge and resilience the dancers have gained in Fiji will provide them with a better sense of self, fresh motivation and the confidence to succeed in both dance and life.

For the Conservatorium of Dance, the reciprocal partnership provides an opportunity for its artists to travel to Canada while also bringing Canadian dancers to Fiji to train, share and learn alongside Fijian students.

Ten of the 15 Canadian dancers are returning to Fiji for their second tour, strengthening the lasting ties between British Columbia and Fiji.

To celebrate this annual cross-cultural partnership, the dancers will present a special Work in Progress Showcase at 6pm tomorrow at the VOU Hub in Nadi, which will be free and open to the public.

Looking ahead, Arch-Way Dance and the VOU Foundation plan to continue their alternating travel schedule, with Fijian artists returning to Canada for future multi-city performance and teaching opportunities.
